lithos_version: lithos 0.5.0 @ a4d2d62; every error envelope below probed against a live Lithos (MCP serverInfo 3.2.0, 2026-10-04) except where observed_divergences says otherwise

request.notes: Applies ONLY to an `open` task: a missing task and a task that is not open are answered with the SAME `task_not_found` code (one code for two facts — the write funnel re-reads the task to tell them apart). Releases every claim on the task. `agent` is the OPERATOR's id, not Lens's: every write auto-registers an unknown agent untyped, which is why the identity guard runs before the funnel calls this. `outcome` is persisted on the task row and forwarded in the `task.completed` event payload; Lens sends it on every completion (the default text names the operator, T3 D7). `cited_nodes` / `misleading_nodes` / `receipt_id` are accepted upstream and never sent — Lens has no node-feedback surface on this path. Every id goes through the SHARED resolver, whose whole domain is probed: a full id (>= 36 characters, a UUID) is handed straight to this tool's own lookup; anything shorter than SIX characters that is not an exact id is `invalid_input`; a 6-to-35-character value is searched as a PREFIX, and matching nothing is the resolver's own `task_not_found` ("No task matches id prefix …", a different message from this tool's own not-found, same code) while matching several is `ambiguous_id_prefix` with up to FIVE `{id, title}` candidate RECORDS — the message states the capped count. Lens sends a full id for this tool (the funnel acts on a task it has just read), so none of the prefix refusals is on a Lens request; all are vendored because the mapper must still answer them.

errors.message: Task 'influx-gate-human' not found or not in an open state.
task_id 'infl' is too short: pass the full task id or a prefix of at least 6 characters.
Task id prefix '506155' (task_id) is ambiguous: 2 or more matches. Retry with a longer prefix or a full id from candidates.

observed_divergences: `unblocked` is a list of task IDS, not records — the payload names only the completed task, so a receipt naming the released tasks has to read them. Everything above is probed live EXCEPT the success payload, which cannot be read without completing a real task: it is transcribed from the tool's own documented return ("Dict with success, unblocked, updated_at, and the resolved task_id + title", `_tools_snapshot.json`). Note the earlier snapshot described it as "Dict with success boolean" only — the four other keys were missed on the first pass of this slice.
